Here's the full path from a typed `@handle` to whatever actually lands in the mentioned person's inbox.

**1. Extraction — `src/lib/mentions.ts`**
Nothing happens at keystroke time in terms of resolution (the composer's `mention-textarea.tsx`/`mention-query.ts` just autocomplete handles for UX). The real extraction happens server-side when the comment is submitted. `extractMentions(body)` in `src/lib/mentions.ts` runs `MENTION_PATTERN` (`/(^|[\s(<[])@([a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,38}[a-z0-9])/gi`) over the body with code spans/fences stripped (`withoutCode`), returning the distinct lowercase handles in first-appearance order.

**2. Handle → real user — `resolveMentions` in the same file, called from `createComment` (`src/server/services/comment-service.ts`)**
`createComment` calls its private `resolveMentionedUsers(orgId, body, clientProvided)`, which fetches up to `MENTION_LOOKUP_LIMIT` (100) org members via `memberRepo.listMembers`, builds a `handle → userId` map using `handleOf(member)` (the lowercased local part of `member.user.email`), and calls `resolveMentions(body, members.items)` to turn the parsed handles into real `UserId`s. Unknown handles are silently dropped. This resolved server-side set is unioned with whatever `UserId`s the client optimistically sent (filtered to only known members), producing the final `mentionedUserIds` array — the server list wins on any disagreement.

**3. What carries the list forward — the `comment.created` event**
`createComment` persists the comment with `mentionedUserIds` via `commentRepo.insertComment`, then calls `emit("comment.created", { ...actorEnvelope(actor), commentId, issueId, mentionedUserIds })` (`src/lib/event-bus`). This event payload is the thing that carries the resolved id list forward — nothing downstream re-parses the markdown.

**4. Fan-out — `registerFanOut` in `src/server/services/notification-service.ts`**
At module load, `registerFanOut()` subscribes to `comment.created`. Its handler first notifies the issue's author/assignee of `comment_created`, then, if `payload.mentionedUserIds.length > 0`, calls `notify(orgId, "comment_mention", payload.mentionedUserIds, { title: "You were mentioned", ... })`.

**5. Per-recipient channel decision — `notify()` and `resolveChannels()`**
For each distinct recipient (skipping the actor mentioning themselves), `notify()` loads that user's `NotificationPreference` via `preferenceRepo.getPreference(orgId, recipientId, "comment_mention")` and calls `resolveChannels(preference, flags)`:
- No stored preference → `DEFAULT_CHANNELS = ["in_app", "email"]` (both).
- A preference exists → `in_app` is included iff `preference.inApp`; `email` is included iff `preference.email` is true AND (`!preference.digestOnly` OR the org's `digest_email` feature flag is enabled via `isEnabled`).
- If the resolved channel list is empty, that recipient is skipped entirely — no row at all.

**6. What actually lands in the inbox**
`notify()` writes one row per recipient (with its own `channels` array) via `notificationRepo.insertNotifications` (`src/server/repositories/notification-repository.ts`) — this is the in-app row, immediately visible in `notification-list.tsx` / the unread badge (`countUnread`).

The `email` entry in `channels` is not itself an immediate send — there is no job that fires a "mention" email right away (the `mention` template in `src/emails/mention-email.tsx` / `src/emails/render.ts` is wired into the render pipeline but nothing currently calls `renderEmail("mention", …)`). Instead, email delivery only happens for users who are digest subscribers: `runDigestEmailJob` (`src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts`) runs per org during its configured UTC hour, calls `digest-service.ts`'s `buildDigest`/`listDigestRecipients` to gather each subscriber's still-unread notifications (`notificationRepo.listUnreadSince`) inside the window, renders them through the generic `"digest"` template, and `sendEmail`s the bundle (which in this offline corpus just logs `"email.sent"` via `email-service.ts`). Digested notifications are then marked read so they aren't re-sent next run.

So the end state for a mentioned user is: always an in-app row (unless every channel was disabled), and email participation depends entirely on their `comment_mention` preference plus the org's `digest_email` flag — non-digest "email" preference currently results in the channel being recorded on the row but no separate immediate email is actually dispatched anywhere in the codebase, while `digestOnly` users get their mention bundled into the next daily digest email.
